# Lause design system

Lause is the design system behind an Estonian-citizenship exam trainer: tokens, components, and the usage rules an AI tool needs before touching this code. This file and components.manifest.json are generated by `npm run build:manifest`. Read them before the source.

## Install and import

`lause-ds` requires Tailwind v4 in the consuming app.

```bash
npm install lause-ds
```

In your Tailwind CSS entry (for example `app/globals.css`), in this order:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import 'lause-ds/styles.css';            /* tokens + the theme; must live here, not in a TSX file */
@source '../node_modules/lause-ds/dist';  /* relative to THIS css file; adjust for src/app/globals.css */
```

Then import components normally:

```tsx
import { Button, Dial, Tile, TileStack } from 'lause-ds';
```

Every component already carries `'use client'`, so it works as it is in a React Server Components app. Load Source Serif 4 and Instrument Sans yourself (Google Fonts, or self-hosted).

To style a plain element the same way the components do, import the shared style constants: `focusRing`, `disabledControl`, `hitTarget`, `hoverFade`, and the `SurfaceState` type (`'idle' | 'selected' | 'filled' | 'dimmed'`) behind `Tile` and `Cell`.

## Tokens

Each line is `token: light · dark | Tailwind utility · CSS custom property | what it is for`. The theme is closed: these utilities exist, anything else (`bg-red-500`, `p-11`) does not.

color.ground: #e3ecf7 (light) · #091727 (dark) | bg-ground / text-ground · --lause-color-ground | page background
color.ink: #0f2238 (light) · #e3ecf7 (dark) | bg-ink / text-ink · --lause-color-ink | text, filled controls
color.dim: #446081 (light) · #95b4d9 (dark) | bg-dim / text-dim · --lause-color-dim | secondary text; solid so contrast is checkable
color.accent: #d93405 (light) · #ff5a36 (dark) | bg-accent / text-accent · --lause-color-accent | graphic accent: underlines, current segment, lit edge
color.accent-text: #a92400 (light) · #ffb19e (dark) | bg-accent-text / text-accent-text · --lause-color-accent-text | accent used as small text
color.accent-on-ink: #ff5a36 (light) · #d93405 (dark) | bg-accent-on-ink / text-accent-on-ink · --lause-color-accent-on-ink | accent on ink fills; full-strength coral reads on navy
color.accent-text-on-ink: #ff5a36 (light) · #a92400 (dark) | bg-accent-text-on-ink / text-accent-text-on-ink · --lause-color-accent-text-on-ink | accent used as small text on ink fills
color.surface: #ffffff (light) · #0f2238 (dark) | bg-surface / text-surface · --lause-color-surface | tiles
color.on-ink: #e3ecf7 (light) · #091727 (dark) | bg-on-ink / text-on-ink · --lause-color-on-ink | text on ink fills
color.ink-hover: #2d4460 (light) · #cddcf0 (dark) | bg-ink-hover / text-ink-hover · --lause-color-ink-hover | hover on ink fills
color.ink-active: #091727 (light) · #b2cae7 (dark) | bg-ink-active / text-ink-active · --lause-color-ink-active | pressed on ink fills
color.ground-hover: #cddcf0 (light) · #0f2238 (dark) | bg-ground-hover / text-ground-hover · --lause-color-ground-hover | hover fill on ground-level controls
color.surface-hover: #f0f6fc (light) · #2d4460 (dark) | bg-surface-hover / text-surface-hover · --lause-color-surface-hover | hover fill on tiles
font.content: Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif (light) · Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif (dark) | font-content · --lause-font-content
font.chrome: Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif (light) · Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif (dark) | font-chrome · --lause-font-chrome
type.label: fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 13px, lineHeight 1.3, fontWeight 600 (light) · fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 13px, lineHeight 1.3, fontWeight 600 (dark) | text-label · --lause-type-label-size
type.body: fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 16px, lineHeight 1.5, fontWeight 400 (light) · fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 16px, lineHeight 1.5, fontWeight 400 (dark) | text-body · --lause-type-body-size
type.title: fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 19px, lineHeight 1.3, fontWeight 600 (light) · fontFamily Instrument Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif, fontSize 19px, lineHeight 1.3, fontWeight 600 (dark) | text-title · --lause-type-title-size
type.reading: fontFamily Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif, fontSize 57px, lineHeight 1.85, fontWeight 600 (light) · fontFamily Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif, fontSize 57px, lineHeight 1.85, fontWeight 600 (dark) | text-reading · --lause-type-reading-size
type.reading-narrow: fontFamily Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif, fontSize 40px, lineHeight 1.85, fontWeight 600 (light) · fontFamily Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif, fontSize 40px, lineHeight 1.85, fontWeight 600 (dark) | text-reading-narrow · --lause-type-reading-narrow-size | reading size for narrow viewports (below 640px)
type.headline: fontFamily Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif, fontSize 83px, lineHeight 1.1, fontWeight 700 (light) · fontFamily Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif, fontSize 83px, lineHeight 1.1, fontWeight 700 (dark) | text-headline · --lause-type-headline-size
type.headline-narrow: fontFamily Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif, fontSize 48px, lineHeight 1.1, fontWeight 700 (light) · fontFamily Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif, fontSize 48px, lineHeight 1.1, fontWeight 700 (dark) | text-headline-narrow · --lause-type-headline-narrow-size | headline size for narrow viewports (below 640px)

## Components

A prop line is `name: ` then the type in backticks, with `= default` inside them when the prop has one, then ` | ` and the doc text, or nothing more when there is none. Read the type as the text between the first backtick and the next: a union's own `|` sits inside those backticks, so it is never mistaken for the separator before the doc text.

### Keycap

A keyboard hint. Inherits its colour, so it follows the text of whatever holds it.

#### Props
- held?: `boolean = false` | Drawn filled while the key is physically held, as ⌥ is during a peek.

States: Default, Held, Row, Dark

Source: packages/ui/src/Keycap/Keycap.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 8:9)

### Button

A pill button. Every control in Lause shows its key, so pass `keycap` whenever there is one.

#### Props
- variant?: `'filled' | 'outline' | 'dim' = 'filled'` | filled: the one primary action. outline: secondary. dim: tertiary, text only.
- keycap?: `string` | The key that triggers this action; drawn as a Keycap after the label.

States: Filled, Hover, DisabledNoHover, Outline, Dim, Disabled, Bar, Dark

#### Rules
- Every control shows its key: pass keycap whenever there is one.
- filled is the one primary action on a screen.
- Disabled controls never hover.

Source: packages/ui/src/Button/Button.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 9:65)

### Progress

The segmented bar under every screen: done in ink, current in accent, the rest faint.

#### Props
- total: `number` | Number of units: sentences, cards, questions, arrows.
- current: `number` | Zero-based index of the current unit. Units before it are done. Pass `total` when everything is done.
- label: `string` | Accessible name, e.g. "Lause 5 / 8".

States: Midway, First, Last, Complete, Exam, Dark

#### Rules
- One segment per unit; the counts are given in words.

Source: packages/ui/src/Progress/Progress.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (component 9:69)

### Bar

Coverage of one domain: one segment per article. Read and retained in ink, read but not retained in accent, unread faint.

#### Props
- segments: `readonly BarSegment[]` | One entry per article, in article order.
- label: `string` | The counts in words, e.g. "Riigikord: 4 kinnistunud, 2 loetud, 4 lugemata, kokku 10". This is the accessible name.

States: Domain, Untouched, Rows, Dark

#### Rules
- One segment per unit; the counts are given in words.

Source: packages/ui/src/Bar/Bar.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (component 9:81)

### Dial

A segmented control that behaves as a radio group: arrow keys move and select, Home/End jump.

#### Props
- options: `readonly DialOption<V>[]` | Two or three positions.
- value: `V`
- onChange: `(value: V) => void`
- label: `string` | Accessible name of the group, e.g. "Tugi".
- disabled?: `boolean = false`

States: Support, Hover, Keyboard, TwoPositions, Disabled, Dark

#### Rules
- The exam disables it as one control.

Source: packages/ui/src/Dial/Dial.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 10:35)

### Tile

An option or word tile. Tiles stack vertically in a TileStack; they never sit in a row except the two of a true/false item.
Drawn as the boards draw the option pills (`LauseExam.png`, `LauseOnboard.png`): the chrome face at the title size, the
keycap on the right edge, tall enough to read as a button, not a row.

#### Props
- state?: `'idle' | 'selected' | 'filled' | 'dimmed' = 'idle'` | idle: available. selected: chosen, accent ring. filled: written in, ink. dimmed: no longer relevant.
- keycap?: `string` | The number key that picks this tile.

States: Idle, Selected, Hover, Filled, Dimmed, Stack, TrueFalse, Dark

#### Rules
- Options stack vertically in a TileStack, never in a row, except the two of a true/false item.
- Options run to 40 characters.

Source: packages/ui/src/Tile/Tile.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 11:69)

### TileStack

The column that holds option tiles: 640px wide at most, one tile per row.

#### Props
- label: `string` | Accessible name of the group, e.g. "Vali õige vastus".

States: Idle, Selected, Hover, Filled, Dimmed, Stack, TrueFalse, Dark

#### Rules
- Options stack vertically in a TileStack, never in a row, except the two of a true/false item.
- Options run to 40 characters.

Source: packages/ui/src/Tile/Tile.tsx

### Bubble

A translation bubble that sits above the word it belongs to. Render it inside an element with
`position: relative`; it centres itself over that element and draws a tail down to it.

#### Props
- children: `ReactNode` | The translation.
- count?: `number` | How many times this term has been looked up; shown as ×N in accent.
- note?: `string` | A short note after the count, e.g. the app's promotion text.
- size?: `'title' | 'body' = 'title'` | title: over reading-size text (the reader). body: over 16 px text, so it covers less of the line above.

States: Pinned, Promoted, NoCount, LongGloss, LongGlossNarrow, Dark, Body, TitleByDefault

#### Rules
- Sits above its word; the count is decorative to assistive technology.

Source: packages/ui/src/Bubble/Bubble.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 42:211)

### Sentence

The reading unit: one sentence at reading size, its neighbours dimmed, its terms openable.

#### Props
- segments: `readonly Segment[]` | The sentence in reading order: plain strings and markable terms.
- previous?: `string` | The neighbours, dimmed above and below.
- next?: `string`
- previousLabel?: `string` | Caps labels over the neighbours, e.g. "eelmine lause" and "järgmine lause", so a reader
knows what the dim lines are. The app passes them in its own language; without them the
neighbours render bare.
- nextLabel?: `string`
- support: `'et' | 'tugi' | 'korvuti'` | The dial level. et: no marks, terms still open. tugi: marks. korvuti: marks and the English under.
- pinned: `readonly string[]` | Term ids whose bubble is shown.
- counts?: `Readonly<Record<string, number>> = {}` | Look-up tally per term id, shown in the bubble.
- notes?: `Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {}` | Per-term note shown after the count, e.g. the promotion text at three look-ups.
- peeking?: `boolean = false` | While true every gloss shows, pinned or not.
Announces nothing; the glosses are already in the accessibility tree and the app decides whether to announce the mode.
- english?: `{ text: string; note: string }` | The Riigi Teataja English and the fixed unofficial-translation line, shown under the sentence
in korvuti; the note is never optional because the text is an unofficial translation of
constitutional law.
- onToggle: `(termId: string) => void` | Called with the term id when a term is clicked or opened with Enter/Space.
- label: `string` | Accessible name of the reading region, e.g. "Lause 5 / 8".

States: Tugi, Gap, GapNarrow, Weight, Keyboard, TwoPins, Peeking, EestiKeeles, Korvuti, RepeatedTerm, Narrow, Dark, LineOffset

#### Rules
- The English pair (text + note) is required together: the note says the translation is unofficial.
- Term ids that repeat pin together.

Source: packages/ui/src/Sentence/Sentence.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 14:322)

### Term

One word that opens its English: marked in Tugi and Kõrvuti, the bubble above it when pinned or peeked.

#### Props
- id: `string` | The term's id; onToggle is called with it.
- text: `string` | The word as written.
- gloss: `string` | Its English, shown in the bubble.
- size: `'reading' | 'body'` | reading: the reader's 40 to 57 px text. body: 16 px text, which keeps the paragraph's font.
- marked: `boolean` | The underline (the Tugi and Kõrvuti levels). Unmarked terms still open on click.
- pinned: `boolean` | The bubble shows and the line turns solid.
- peeking?: `boolean = false` | While true the bubble shows, pinned or not.
- count?: `number` | Look-up tally, shown in the bubble.
- note?: `string` | Shown after the count, e.g. the promotion text at three look-ups.
- onToggle: `(id: string) => void` | Called with the id when the term is clicked or opened with Enter or Space.

States: BodyIdle, BodyPinned, BodyGap, BodyInheritsFont, ReadingIdle, ReadingPinned, Unmarked, Peeked, Dark

#### Rules
- The line sits 4 px under the letters at both sizes.
- Body size keeps the paragraph font; reading size is the content font.
- Unmarked terms (Eesti keeles) still open on click.

Source: packages/ui/src/Term/Term.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 7:48)

### TermText

A run of text with its terms, inline, with no element of its own: the caller's <p> or <li> keeps
its layout. It announces each newly pinned gloss in a polite live region.

#### Props
- segments: `readonly Segment[]` | The text in reading order: plain strings and terms.
- size: `'reading' | 'body'` | reading: Sentence's 40 to 57 px text. body: 16 px text in the caller's font.
- support: `'et' | 'tugi' | 'korvuti'` | The dial level. et: no marks, terms still open. tugi and korvuti: marks.
- pinned: `readonly string[]` | Term ids whose bubble is shown.
- counts?: `Readonly<Record<string, number>> = {}` | Look-up tally per term id, shown in the bubble.
- notes?: `Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {}` | Per-term note shown after the count.
- peeking?: `boolean = false` | While true every gloss shows, pinned or not.
- onToggle: `(termId: string) => void` | Called with the term id when a term is clicked or opened with Enter or Space.

States: Tugi, EestiKeeles, SharedId, NoWrapperElement

#### Rules
- Renders inline with no element of its own: put it inside the caller's <p> or <li>.
- Term ids that repeat pin together.

Source: packages/ui/src/TermText/TermText.tsx

### usePeek

The peek gesture: hold the modifier and every translation shows; release and it goes.
A latch holds the same state without the key. The held modifier clears when the window
loses focus or is hidden; the latch is the app's and survives blur. The modifier's keydown
is cancelled so it cannot move focus to the browser's menu bar.

#### Props
- latched?: `boolean = false` | The latch: holds the peek on without the key.
- key?: `string = 'Alt'` | The modifier that peeks while held.
- enabled?: `boolean = true` | Set false to register no listeners and report `held: false`, e.g. while the reader is off-screen.

Source: packages/ui/src/usePeek/usePeek.ts

### Nav

The top chrome: context left, caps navigation centre, controls right.

#### Props
- context: `ReactNode` | Top-left: where the learner is, e.g. "§ 60 · lause 5 / 8".
- items: `readonly NavItem[]` | The centre items. Empty in exam mode.
- current?: `string` | The current item's id.
- peeking?: `boolean = false` | While true the items read their English labels. The chrome swaps; it never gains a subtitle.
- controls?: `ReactNode` | Top-right: the dial and the peek hint, or the exam's one action.
- label: `string` | Accessible name of the navigation.
- onNavigate?: `(id: string) => void` | Supply this when the app owns routing. A plain left-click then calls it with the item id and
suppresses the browser's own navigation; modifier and middle clicks still open the link.
Leave it out and the links navigate by themselves.

States: Reader, Peeking, Exam, Dark

#### Rules
- Chrome stays Estonian; while peeking it swaps to English and never gains a subtitle.

Source: packages/ui/src/Nav/Nav.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 15:71)

### Cell

One cell of the 2×2 drill: the subject, the verdict, and its key.

#### Props
- subject: `string` | The row's subject, e.g. "Igaüks".
- verdict?: `string` | The column's verdict, e.g. "tohib piirata".
- keycap?: `string` | The number key that picks this cell.
- state?: `'idle' | 'selected' | 'filled' | 'dimmed' = 'idle'`

States: Idle, Selected, Filled, Dimmed, Grid, Dark

#### Rules
- Rows Igaüks / Eesti kodanik, columns Tohib piirata / Ei tohi piirata; keys 1–4.

Source: packages/ui/src/Cell/Cell.tsx
Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/Fi9CrQ0KzJdpCuwNcWbZKF (set 16:101)

### CellGrid

The 2×2 drill laid out as a table, so the headers are read with each cell.

#### Props
- rows: `readonly [string, string]` | The two row headers, top to bottom.
- columns: `readonly [string, string]` | The two column headers, left to right.
- label: `string` | Accessible name of the table.
- children: `readonly [ReactNode, ReactNode, ReactNode, ReactNode]` | Exactly four cells, in reading order: row 1 left, row 1 right, row 2 left, row 2 right.
- className?: `string`

States: Idle, Selected, Filled, Dimmed, Grid, Dark

#### Rules
- Rows Igaüks / Eesti kodanik, columns Tohib piirata / Ei tohi piirata; keys 1–4.

Source: packages/ui/src/Cell/Cell.tsx

## Rules

- Use only token utilities: the Tailwind theme is closed, so bg-red-500 or p-11 do not exist.
- Two fonts only: font-content (Source Serif 4) for what is being learned, font-chrome (Instrument Sans) for the app.
- Type is used through the roles (label, body, title, reading, headline, display, and reading-narrow / headline-narrow below 640px), never a size number.
- Contrast is a gate: every text pair 4.5:1, every graphic pair 3:1, in both modes.
- Hit targets are at least 44px.
- Every interactive element has a visible focus ring; disabled never hovers.
